facts.statement: GIFT City, Gandhinagar spans 886 acres (261 SEZ + 625 DTA) with planned 62 million sq ft BUA (67% commercial, 22% residential, 11% social), and is expanding from 886 to 3,300+ acres; it was conceived in 2007 by the then Chief Minister Narendra Modi and is developed/operated by GIFTCL.
facts.detail: Infrastructure: District Cooling System (30% energy savings), Automated Waste Collection System, underground utility tunnel ('Digging Free City'), 24x7 potable water, zero-discharge city; metro operationalised July 2024.

facts.statement: Setting up an IFSC unit takes 8 steps: identify space, incorporate the entity, obtain Provisional LoA from the developer, file Form-FA to the SEZ Administrator (IFSCA), apply to IFSCA for the sector licence, obtain Final LoA from the UAC chaired by the Administrator, execute the lease, and take regulatory approval to commence; steps 4 and 5 are merged via the SWIT (Single Window IT System) portal, while non-IFSC SEZ units use Form-F to the Development Commissioner.
facts.detail: With effect from 28 February 2024, certain Development Commissioner SEZ powers were vested in IFSCA.

facts.statement: IFSC tax framework: 100% income-tax exemption for 10 consecutive years out of 15; MAT/AMT at 9% of book profits (not applicable if the new tax regime is opted); no STT, CTT or stamp duty on IFSC exchange transactions; no GST on services received/provided within IFSC or to offshore clients.

Companies Act relaxations for IFSC companies: first Board meeting within 60 days of incorporation and at least one meeting per half-year (instead of quarterly); CSR not applicable for 5 years; no Audit Committee or Nomination & Remuneration Committee required; managerial remuneration limits not applicable; EGM may be held anywhere with shareholder approval; the financial year may match the holding company without approval.

Gujarat state subsidies for GIFT City: capital subsidy 25% of CAPEX (max INR 2,000 million for investments above INR 2,500 million, otherwise max INR 500 million); operating subsidy 15% for 5 years; 100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years; EPF reimbursement 100% for female and 75% for male employees; interest subsidy up to 7% for 5 years capped at INR 10 million per year.

GFCI rankings: GIFT IFSC ranked 46th in GFCI 37 (March 2025) with the top five being New York, London, Hong Kong, Singapore and San Francisco; GIFT IFSC rose to 43rd by September 2025; India targets a top-30 position by 2030; GIFT City was ranked 1st for potential significance in the GFCI September 2020 report.
facts.detail: Global Innovation Index 2025: India 38th; IMD World Competitiveness 2025: India 41st of 69.

facts.statement: IFSC entity trajectory: 628+ entities (May 2024), 766 registrations (Dec-2024), 865 (Mar-2025, total registrations 864 in annual report), 939 (Jun-2025), 1,034 (Sep-2025), 1,100 (Dec-2025); June-2025 composition: 25 banks (9 foreign), 3 exchanges (India INX, IIBX, NSE IFSC), 26 aircraft leasing firms, 80 fund managers and 40 fintechs.

IBU economics trajectory: 12 IBUs and USD 14,977 million assets (FY21), 15/USD 29,381 million (FY22), 20/USD 38,286 million (FY23), 23/USD 60,248 million (FY24), 28 IBUs + 2 GAOs with USD 88.51 billion assets (FY25), reaching USD 106.33 billion assets, gross credit USD 74.18 billion and deposits USD 8.63 billion by December 2025.
facts.detail: FY25: customer credit USD 59.46 billion (+52% YoY); cumulative transactions USD 448.49 billion; derivatives USD 398.36 billion; 15 specified foreign currencies (SEK, NOK, NZD, DKK added); country exposure Dec-25: India 74.54%, USA 5.44%, Singapore 2.82%; sector credit: services 52%, manufacturing 20%, infrastructure 14%.

facts.statement: Under the Foreign University Regulations 2022, top-ranked global institutions may set up IFSC campuses offering finance, fintech and STEM programs; four universities operate - Deakin University, University of Wollongong, Coventry University and Queen's University (Deakin was the first).

Finance company sector: 74 registered (FY25); ITFS transactions USD 44.36 million; GRCTC loans USD 2,332 million with investments USD 141.38 million; December-2025: ITFS 2,106 transactions/USD 87.37 million, GRCTC loans USD 4.03 billion/investments USD 234.45 million, Core Finance Company loans USD 33.72 million/investments USD 80.97 million.
facts.detail: GRCTC functions: centralized cash management, intercompany lending, commodity trading, hedging, reinvoicing; IOC Global Capital Management was the first GRCTC and OVL Overseas IFSC the second.

facts.statement: FinTech ecosystem data (FY25): 18 direct authorisations, 27 sandbox entities, 23 exits, 88 ancillary service providers employing about 610 professionals, and 3 BATF entities; December-2025: sandbox 7 entities with 43 exits, FSS entities (incl. TechFin/BATF/GIC) 143; TAS entities 133 (Sep-2025).

IFSCA's stated themes: GIFT IFSC as a trusted cross-border finance platform; principle-based regulation with risk-based supervision; a two-fold mandate - regulate with integrity and develop with vision - aligned to Viksit Bharat@2047; a forthcoming Consumer Charter alongside the Stewardship Code.
